questions.q: What three parts make up a simple Power Automate condition?
options: A trigger, an action, and an approval
A value, an operator, and a comparison value
A loop, a count, and a timeout
A connector, a template, and an environment
questions.explain: Every simple condition compares one value against another using an operator, such as 'is equal to' or 'is greater than' — a three-part shape.

questions.q: In a flow with a condition, how many branches execute during a single run?
options: Both If yes and If no always run
Neither branch runs unless manually triggered
Exactly one of the two branches runs, based on whether the condition was true or false
All branches run in parallel regardless of the result
questions.explain: A condition evaluates to true or false, and the flow executes only the matching branch — If yes or If no — never both.

questions.q: Castlebridge's shipping flow needs to check that a shipment was BOTH approved AND worth over $10,000 before sending a special high-value notice. What should replace the simple three-box condition?
options: Two separate unconnected conditions with no relationship
An expression using and() to combine both checks into a single true/false result
A loop that repeats the check until it passes
Nothing — the three-box condition can already check two values at once
questions.explain: The simple three-box condition only handles one comparison. Combining two checks requires an expression using and(), or(), or not().

questions.q: In the If yes / If no branches of a condition, how are the actions in each branch related?
options: They share the exact same configuration automatically
Each branch is configured completely independently, with its own separate set of actions
If no branch can contain more than one action
If no actions are allowed in the If no branch
questions.explain: If yes and If no are independent branches — actions added to one have no effect on the other, and each must be configured separately.

questions.q: Which operator would correctly check whether an approver's response equals "Approve"?
options: contains
is greater than
is equal to
starts with
questions.explain: 'Is equal to' is the operator used to test an exact match, such as checking whether the Approver response value is exactly 'Approve'.
